newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on exports.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed with nearby months higher on USDA weekly exports and talk an Argentine firm cut its Argentine soybean production figure, traders said.

Renewed interest in July/November spreading also boosted nearbys, powered by ideas old crop supplies would run out while new crop acreage should jump. The July/November spread tacked on 4-1/2 cents to close at $1.53, premium July.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans were at 298,900 tonnes.
Traders said the weekly export pace, while in line with expectations, was too high given tight stocks. Exports need to fall below 200,000 tonnes to preserve supplies, they said.

Floor sources pointed to talk an Argentine firm pegged Argentine's soybean production this year at 11.0 million to 11.5 million tonnes, below USDA's expectations for 13.25 million tonnes but above some estimates for 10 million tonnes.
Soybeans ended 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 2-1/2 cents lower with May up 4-1/2 at $8.47.
The Census Bureau's monthly oil crush report showed the soy crush within expectations at 130.092 million bushels but above February's crush of 125.132 million.
Some floor sources said the Census oilmill stocks data was supportive. That figure showed oilmill stocks at roughly 105 million bushels, below the February figure of 122 million.

"The ownership figures off the Census crush were supportive," Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co said. "With only 105 million on hand, that will tighten the basis up. Guys are concentrating on planting and it's getting harder to buy cash (soybeans)."
On the day, Refco Inc bought three million bushels July, Tenco Inc and ADM each bought 1.5 million July and ING bought 1.3 million July, pit sources said.
Tenco Inc spread 1.6 million bushels May/JUly at 1-1/2 to 1-1/4 cents, premium July, and Produce Grain spread 1.5 million May/July at one cent, premium July.
In options, Lind-Waldock bought 900 July $8.75 calls at 22-1/2 cents and sold 900 July $9.25 calls at 12 cents. Lind also bought 200 July $8.00 puts at 11-1/2 cents.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 46,223 contracts.
